dossier.public_summary: TESS shows two deep eclipses of equal depth ~5360 ppm every 0.65 days, plus a strong phase curve, on a 0.19 solar-radius M dwarf. The secondary eclipse and out-of-eclipse variation match a stellar binary, not a planet. The signal is centred on the target star, so it is an eclipsing binary on the target.

reasons.why: A second dip at phase 0.6603 with ~91% of the primary depth and SNR 30.76 is far above the brightenings. This is the classic secondary eclipse of a stellar companion; a planet would show no eclipse at this size even allowing a hot giant.
A coherent out-of-eclipse swing of ~6200 ppm comparable to the transit depth indicates ellipsoidal/reflection variability of an eclipsing binary, not a quiet planet transit.
Duration is ~1.8x the central duration for the 0.1865 Rsun M dwarf, with high impact parameter; density mismatch shows the light curve is not a planet transiting a density-consistent host.

Difference imaging puts the dip on the target with no plausible neighbour within 1px (plausible_within_1px=0), so the false-positive is not a blended eclipsing binary but an eclipsing binary on the target itself.
